episodes.156906: A lone thunderstorm in the morning uprooted numerous trees in parts of Polk County. More widespread thunderstorms in afternoon produced multiple reports of funnel clouds, hail and wind damage. Two brief tornadoes were also reported.
episodes.157001: Scattered showers and thunderstorms redeveloped during the evening of May 10th across portions of extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas, ahead of another upper level disturbance that ejected east across the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and North Texas. These elevated storms developed well north of a shallow cold front which settled south into portions of Southeast Texas and Central Louisiana, where steep lapse rates aloft contributed to adequate instability such that a few of these storms become severe, producing large hail. One such severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail near Ringold in Southwest McCurtain County before the storms diminished during the late evening hours.
episodes.157025: A shallow cold front which moved through the Four State Region on May 9th lifted back north as a warm front into portions of Lower East Texas south of Interstate 20 during the day of the 11th. Meanwhile, an upper level disturbance shifted east along the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and North Texas north of the front, enhancing scattered shower and thunderstorm development over portions of extreme Northeast Texas, Southeast Oklahoma, and Southwest Arkansas. Given the steep lapse rates which promoted moderate instability aloft ahead of the trough, an isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Sevier County Arkansas during the early morning hours, producing quarter size hail in De Queen before weakening a short time later.
episodes.157026: A shallow cold front which moved through the Four State Region on May 9th lifted back north as a warm front into portions of Lower East Texas south of Interstate 20 during the afternoon of the 11th, with warm, humid, and unstable air spilling back north into this area ahead of an upper trough that shifted east into the Central and Southern Plains. This trough and associated large scale forcing contributed to a large area of elevated showers and thunderstorms that developed over West Texas during the morning, and spread east into East Texas during the mid and late afternoon. These storms became more surface based as they moved into the warm sector of Lower East Texas, and quickly became severe, producing damaging winds and large hail. However, the storms quickly weakened by late afternoon as they moved back into a more stable air mass near and east of the Sabine River into North Louisiana, but continued to produce widespread moderate to heavy rainfall before exiting the area during the early and mid evening hours.
episodes.157124: A surface area of low pressure tracked from the high plains crossing northern Ohio on Sunday May 9th. Widespread light to moderate rain developed Sunday morning and was ongoing through much of the day. Temperatures were in the upper 30s to low 40s, and some snowflakes mixed in midday. As the system moved east, rain turned to snow in the primary snowbelt with reports up to 2��� in northwest Pennsylvania and Geauga County Ohio. ||Total rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches were observed over a large swath of the area. Despite mild drought conditions, a recent rain event had contributed to increasing soil moisture. Runoff resulted in flooding over a dozen rivers and creeks, with moderate flooding observed on the Eagle Creek at Findlay, Scioto River at La Rue, and Sandusky River at La Rue.
episodes.157205: Slow moving thunderstorms brought around 6 inches of rain in just a few hours to portions of Decatur county, resulting in flash flooding.  In addition, a few trees were blown down in portions of Colquitt and Worth counties.
episodes.157206: Scattered thunderstorms brought a few impacts to the Florida panhandle with a report of a power line blown down in Calhoun county, as well as lightning striking a road in Walton county.
episodes.157615: A quasi-stationary front meandered north of the local area with zonal flow aloft. A dominant west coast sea breeze regime focused higher thunderstorm potential across the eastern portion of NE FL in the afternoon and evening hours, with a few pulse severe storms producing lightning and some wind damage near sea breeze and outflow boundary mergers.
episodes.157652: A surface front draped across the middle of South Carolina during the afternoon provided the focus for isolated severe thunderstorm development as an upper level trough provided support. A severe thunderstorm complex developed near St. Matthews, and traveled SE over Lake Marion.
episodes.157907: A weak trough was over the Rocky Mountains. A cold front from the previous day was across the Lower Trans Pecos which helped to provide atmospheric lift. High moisture and instability were present along the front. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms with large hail developing and moving across Terrell County in Texas.
episodes.158080: A cold front and moderate to strong instability resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms across the Heartland and Northwest Hill Country. The storms produced large to very large hail.
episodes.158354: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northern Texas and southeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 10th, north of a warm front that stretched across central Texas. The combination of elevated instability and wind shear supported the development of a supercell thunderstorm, which moved across Choctaw County and produced hail up to baseball size.
episodes.158428: Thunderstorms tracked along the Red River during the morning hours of the 10th, with several reports of large hail received.
episodes.158429: A weak upper wave and an unstable airmass led to widespread showers and thunderstorms, with a few strong storms producing marginally severe hail across southern OK during the morning of the 11th.
episodes.158591: Isolated thunderstorms developed near a stationary boundary in the late afternoon across interior southeast Georgia. One of these storms produced hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.158592: Isolated thunderstorms developed near a stationary boundary in the early evening across southeast South Carolina. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.158662: Though a cold front had already pushed through the area, a strong upper level disturbance led to the development of strong and severe thunderstorms on Monday May 10 in the cool sector north of the front. Large hail occurred in several locations mainly along and north of the Interstate 20 corridor.
episodes.158822: A cold front moved into the region during stalled during the morning of the 11th. Diurnal heating combined with high moisture and a disturbance aloft allowed scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop with some becoming severe.
episodes.158918: A cold front moved into east Texas causing scattered thunderstorms. One storm became severe.
episodes.158923: An upper level shortwave trough moved across a stationary front and generated thunderstorms over the western part of South Central Texas and northern Mexico. Some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.158924: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front over South Central Texas for a third straight day. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.159173: A moist and moderately unstable atmosphere along and ahead of a stationary front across central Georgia resulted in isolated strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.159212: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina Piedmont during the evening. At least one of the storms produced hail in Iredell County.
episodes.159343: Scattered strong to severe storms formed just ahead of a cold front which moved into northern and western portions of central North Carolina during the early afternoon, before pushing southeast through central North Carolina through mid evening. Several of the storms produced damaging winds and large hail. The strongest supercell produced an |EF-1 tornado in southern portions of Alamance County.

An average of two inches of rain fell over Wyandot County and the Tymochtee Creek on May 9th resulting in minor flooding. The USGS river gage at Crawford reported a crest of 8.5 feet on the 11th. The relatively flat land and slow runoff displaced the flooding to nearly 24 hours after the rain ended over the area. Numerous County Highways were flooded including CH 16 flooded east of State Route 53 north of Tymotchee. Other County Highways that were inundated include CH 35, 4, 16, 37, 38, 42, 47, and 53.
